children: reported a near 28% fall in second-quarter profit on Tuesday, as higher costs for raw materials overshadowed strong demand for its tyres.
The Wanderer-tyre maker's profit fell to 3.69 billion rupees ($39.29 million) in the quarter ended September 30, from 5.12 billion rupees a year earlier.
Revenue from operations rose by almost 18% to 85.24 billion rupees, while total expenses grew by more than 22%, driven largely by a rise in material costs related to war in the Middle East
Cost of materials consumed grew by about 44% during the quarter
Demand for tyres remained resilient in the July-September quarter, supported by steady dispatches from automakers

Indian tyre makers faced higher raw material costs during the quarter as supply shortages and adverse weather in key producing countries kept natural rubber prices elevated, forcing companies to raise prices
MRF, which makes tyres certified by Suzuki
for use in its superbikes, declared an interim dividend of three rupees per share for the financial year ending March 31
reported lower second-quarter earnings as higher raw material prices squeezed margins
